newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand plans measures to revive property sector.
newsitem.headline: Thailand plans measures to revive property sector.

text.p: Thailand plans to launch soon measures to rescue the nation's battered property sector, central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said.

The measures include setting up a new institution, providing soft loans and tax cuts, he said, adding that a top priority was to restore investor confidence in the accuracy of recent data on non-performing loans in the property sector.
"Although the central bank disclosed the non-performing loans level of commercial banking industry late last year, investors seemed reluctant to accept it," he told reporters.

According to the Bank of Thailand's figures released in December, non-performing loans of Thai commercial banks averaged only 7.73 percent of outstanding loans at end-June. The figure was lower than that posted by Malaysia and Indonesia.
Rerngchai said that as a long-term measure, the government would push to establish a secondary mortgage corporation to provide the loans.

Short-term measures to boost demand included providing 20 billion baht ($800 million) soft loans to government and state-enterprise officials wishing to buy their first apartments or homes in which they intend to live and not sell for profit.
The government also plans to exempt capital gain taxes within this year for those selling houses and apartments.
The depressed Thai property sector is facing a slump due to oversupply and weak cash flows.
The economic slowdown coupled with the prolonged property sector slump have sparked fears that loan defaults in the property sector would hit financial institutions.
Another long-term measure to help the property sector included setting up a private institution to buy real estate projects from troubled financial institutions and manage them, Rerngchai said.
He said details of the scheme were being discussed with the Thai Bankers Association. -- Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
